status: electronic prototype development; no populated board tested

adc.avdd: Nominal 5 V analog supply, filtered per bridge
adc.reference: ADC reference connected to the corresponding E+ feed after the current shunt and to E- at the board; calibrate the complete four-wire bridge and cable
adc.clock_note: A two-instruction RP2040 PIO loop at an integer clock divider drives both ADCs from one clock. Actual clock integrity, rate and synchronization require scope checks.

current_monitors.location: One shunt in each E+ feed; the same board-side excitation feeds the ADC reference

electrical_self_test.connection: Switch the resistor between E+ and S+ to shunt bridge R1
electrical_self_test.control: 3.3 V GPIO, active high; each SEL has a 100 kohm pull-down
electrical_self_test.mode: Explicit startup diagnostic; no taring of measured force
limits: An electrical shunt response does not prove gauge bonding or force sensitivity.
Lead-fault coverage and response thresholds must be checked on physical boards.
A signal-pair short may be indistinguishable from a real zero between self-tests.

analog_input.bias: AINP weakly biased to analog supply; AINN weakly biased to GND. Connected-bridge offset is removed only by physical calibration.

bridge_cable.requirement: Measure cable resistance and calibrate with the complete installed cable. Keep E+/E- and S+/S- as twisted pairs.
bridge_cable.note: Cable resistance contributes to gain and temperature sensitivity. Verify it in the physical comparison; the force calibration is specific to the installed assembly.

analog_notes: Keep the ground plane continuous; put analog bridge connections near their ADCs.
Route the clock away from high-gain inputs and use source series termination.
Keep the Pico and digital connector close; verify clock waveforms on the actual assembly.
Use twisted excitation and signal pairs, with shield termination at the fixed electronics. Keep bridge cables and their strain relief out of the mechanical load path.
